text:
Photo Comments
> Leave text feedback directly on any photo in Zuper and @mention teammates to pull them into the conversation.

Commenting on photos in Zuper lets you leave text feedback directly on any photo. You can @mention teammates to pull them into the conversation. Mentioned users receive an in-app notification that takes them straight to the photo and comment. This keeps all photo-related feedback in one place, so nothing gets lost.

You can comment on any photo in Zuper, whether it was uploaded directly to the Gallery, added via a Checklist or Note, or attached to a record.

metadata.title: Photo Comments

text:
Photo Comments > Adding a Comment
**Web**

    1. Open any photo in Zuper. The photo opens with a **Details** and **Comments** panel on the right.
    2. Click the comment input field at the bottom of the panel and type your message.
    3. To add an emoji, click the  icon in the comment toolbar and select from the picker.
    4. To notify a teammate, type **@** and select their name from the dropdown. The photo uploader appears first, followed by all other users alphabetically.

Note:
      Comments are plain text only. Rich text and file attachments are not supported.

    5. Click  **Post**. Your comment appears in the thread, and the mentioned users are notified instantly.

**Mobile**

    1. Open any photo in Zuper.
    2. Tap the **Comments** button at the bottom right of the screen.

    3. Type your message in the input field.
    4. To notify a teammate, type **@** and select their name from the dropdown.
    5. Tap **Post** . Your comment appears in the thread, and the mentioned users are notified instantly.

metadata.title: Photo Comments > Adding a Comment

text:
Photo Comments > Notifications
When you @mention a teammate in a comment, they receive an in-app notification. Tapping the notification opens the comment along with the associated photo.

Identifying Photos with Comments
In the Gallery, photos that already have comments show a **comment count badge**  on the thumbnail. The badge displays the total number of comments on that photo. Click the photo to open it and read the full comment thread.

metadata.title: Photo Comments > Notifications

text:
Photo Comments > Editing or Deleting a Comment
To edit or delete a comment, click the context menu **(...)** next to your comment and select **Edit** or **Delete**. You can only edit or delete comments you wrote. Admins can also delete comments posted by Field Technicians.

Frequently asked questions
**Where can I access photo comments?**

    You can comment on any photo in Zuper — whether it was uploaded directly to the Gallery, added via a Checklist or Note, or attached to a record.

**How do I know if a photo already has comments?**

    In the Gallery, photos with comments show a comment count badge on the thumbnail. The number tells you how many comments have been posted on that photo. Click the photo to open it and read the full thread. For photos added via Checklists, Notes, or Attachments, open the photo directly to view comments.

**Can I reply to a specific comment?**

    Not in this version. Comments appear as a flat chronological list.

metadata.title: Photo Comments > Editing or Deleting a Comment

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper
> Connect Gmail or Outlook to Zuper, and work customer email against the job or customer it belongs to.

Every job and every customer conversation eventually needs an email. Zuper connects the Gmail or Outlook mailbox your team already uses. Email then becomes part of the same record as calls, texts, and job details. It no longer lives in a separate inbox.

You start by creating an inbox. An inbox can be personal, for one user, or shared, for a whole team. Either kind can bring in only Zuper-related mail, or your entire mailbox. Once you connect a mailbox, emails link to the right customer. Your team then replies without leaving Zuper.

You see and manage this email everywhere your team already works. Use the **Communication** module for a unified inbox across your business. Use the **Communication** tab on a job or customer record for that record's own history. This article helps you get started. For the full set of steps once you are up and running, see the related articles at the end of this page.

Note:
  Learn more about how connected emails appear on jobs and customer records in **Emails in jobs and contacts**.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes
There are two kinds of inbox, and different people create each one.

* **Personal inbox**: Each user connects their own mailbox. It appears only for that user, unless someone shares it.
* **Shared inbox**: An admin creates this inbox, and grants access to the roles or users who need it. Sharing happens inside Zuper, not with the mailbox provider, so the account type does not restrict it. A Microsoft shared mailbox, a Google Workspace account, or a personal Gmail or Outlook address can all become a shared inbox.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes > Setup steps
You authenticate a personal inbox from your own user account in the **Communication** module. Only an admin can create a shared inbox.

1. Select **Personal** or **Shared** as the inbox type.
2. Enter a name for the inbox. This name is a label inside Zuper, separate from the email address. Choose a name your team recognizes at a glance, since it appears in the inbox list.
3. Select **Zuper-only** or **Fully synced** as the setup option. See the table below for what each option syncs. This choice affects everything a user sees, so confirm it before you grant access.
4. Select the roles or users who get access to the inbox. A personal inbox that stays private needs no action here.
5. Set permissions for each role or user you added to a shared inbox. See the permissions table below.
6. Select **Save and Connect** to connect the mailbox through Google or Microsoft. Whoever completes this step must be able to sign in to the mailbox. For a shared mailbox, this is usually the admin who owns it or has delegated access. Sync begins once you complete this step.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes > Setup steps

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes > Setup options
| Option | What syncs | Use for |
| - | - | - |
| **Zuper-only** | Only emails linked to a job or customer. Zuper does not sync Sent, Drafts, Spam, or other folders and labels. | Personal mailboxes, and mailboxes where most mail is unrelated to Zuper. |
| **Fully synced** | Your entire mailbox, including standard folders such as Sent, Drafts, and Spam, plus any custom folders or labels. If you create a folder in Zuper, it syncs back to your Gmail or Outlook account. | A dedicated shared inbox for customer work. |

Note:
  A fully synced inbox also allows **Move to Spam**, **Report spam**, and **New label** actions, along with bulk trash and spam actions. A Zuper-only inbox does not support these actions.

Tip:
  Select **Zuper-only** when you share a personal mailbox. A fully synced inbox would let colleagues read everything in it.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes > Setup options

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes > Permissions
Set permissions per inbox, for roles or for individual users. Settings on an individual user override the settings from their role.

| Control | What it does |
| - | - |
| **View** | See the inbox, and read its emails, within the setup option chosen in step three. |
| **Send** | Send email from the inbox. Since View is required, you cannot grant Send alone. |
| **Notifications** | Get alerts for incoming email in the inbox. |

A user can have no access, View only, or View and Send access. You can turn on Notifications alongside either access level.

Warning:
  Provider permissions do not carry over. Granting someone access to a shared mailbox in Microsoft or Google grants them nothing in Zuper, until you set View here. Removing their access at the provider does not remove their Zuper access either. Manage access in both places independently.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Creating inboxes > Permissions

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > The communication module
**Path:** **Communication**

**Conversations** is one queue across all your customers. It lists text messages and emails from everyone, together. If Zuper Connect is enabled, email sits alongside texts and calls. A new email then arrives as a conversation, and you reply to it the same way you reply to a text.

Use **Conversations** to see what needs a response right now. Use a job's or customer's own **Communication** tab, covered next, when you want the history for one record.

Select **Mark as Closed** on a conversation once it is handled. The conversation reopens automatically if the customer replies. Select the checkboxes on several conversations to use the bulk **Mark as read** and **Mark as closed** actions.

Select the **Open** dropdown, or the filter icon, to filter by **Needs Attention**, **Unread**, or **Unresponded**.

The **Emails** tab gives you the same context, focused on email only. It lists every inbox you have access to, personal and shared, and you view one at a time. Use this tab when texts and calls would be noise.

Note:
  Search works on the subject line only.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > The communication module

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Linking emails to contacts and jobs
Linking is what makes an email appear on the job or customer record. Without it, the email exists only in the inbox.

* **Automatic linking**: An incoming email from an address already saved on a customer links to that customer as soon as it arrives. Zuper does not link the job automatically.
* **Manual linking**: Select **Add contact** and **Add job** below the message body while composing. You can also do this at the top of an email you already sent or received. If you link a contact first, Zuper offers only that contact's jobs.
* **Changing a link**: Select the three-dot menu on a chip, then select **Change** or **Remove**.

Tip:
  Linking a contact or job also unlocks email templates and job or customer custom fields in the composer.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Linking emails to contacts and jobs

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Communication within jobs and contacts
**Path:** **Jobs** > a job > **Communication**, or **Contacts** > a customer > **Communication**

Every job and customer record has its own **Communication** tab, alongside **Details**, **Notes**, and **Gallery**. Three views sit inside this tab.

**All Messages** is the unified console for that record. With Zuper Connect enabled, emails and texts appear together, so you never check two places for one conversation. Select **All Inboxes** to combine every number and mailbox, or filter to just one.

**Emails** narrows the view to email for that record only. On a job, the **Show Related** toggle switches between this job's email and everything linked to the customer.

**Activity** logs every email sent from the record. This differs from the other two views in an important way: **Emails** and **All Messages** show only the inboxes you have access to, while **Activity** shows every email sent from the record. Anyone with access to the record can open the full thread from **Activity**, even without access to the inbox it came from.

Note:
  **Activity** shows every email sent from the record, even from inboxes you do not have access to. **Emails** and **All Messages** show only the inboxes you can see.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Communication within jobs and contacts

text:
Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Attachments in emails
You can attach a file to an email from your device, from a gallery, or from job documents. What you can attach depends on what the email is linked to.

| Source | Requires |
| - | - |
| From device | Nothing |
| From gallery | A linked contact or job |
| From job document | A linked job |

FAQs
**What happens if I do not link an email to a job or customer?**

    The email stays in the inbox, but does not appear anywhere else. Linking is what makes an email show up on a job or customer record.

**Can I see an email from an inbox I do not have access to?**

    Only through a record's **Activity** view. **Activity** shows every email sent from a job or customer, even from inboxes you cannot see. **Emails** and **All Messages** show only the inboxes you have access to.

**If I grant someone access to a shared mailbox in Google or Microsoft, do they get access in Zuper too?**

    No. Zuper permissions and mailbox provider permissions work independently. Set **View** for that person in Zuper as well, or they will not see the inbox.

**What does a Zuper-only inbox sync?**

    Only emails linked to a job or customer. Standard folders such as Sent, Drafts, and Spam, and any custom folders or labels, do not sync.

**Can I grant someone Send access without View access?**

    No. View is required before you can grant Send, since a user needs to see the inbox to send from it.

metadata.title: Getting Started with Email in Zuper > Attachments in emails

text:
Photo Annotation
In Zuper, the **Photo Editor** transforms your ordinary images into precise, professional visuals that eliminate guesswork and drive faster decisions.

Whether you need to highlight damage, point out specific issues, add accurate measurements, flag areas for attention, or create compelling before-and-after documentation, the editor lets you annotate directly within Zuper. There is no need for external tools, downloads, or re-uploads.

Every change is saved seamlessly to the relevant record, keeping your visual documentation accurate, contextual, and immediately accessible to everyone on the team.

The editor is available across four modules: **Jobs**, **Projects**, **Customers**, and **Properties**.

metadata.title: Photo Annotation

text:
Photo Annotation > Before you begin
Ensure at least one photo is available in the record before opening the editor.

Note:
  **Note**: The editor works on images only. Videos cannot be annotated.

Accessing the Photo Editor
You can open the editor from either the ***Gallery*** tab or the ***Attachments*** section of any supported record:

1. Navigate to the desired **Job, Project, Customer, or Property** record.
2. In the left navigation panel of the record, click the **Gallery** tab (or **Attachments** section).

3. Click the image you want to annotate. It opens in full-screen view.

4. Click **Open Editor** in the top-right corner of the viewer.

The **Photo Editor** opens with the selected image on the canvas and an annotation toolbar on the left.

metadata.title: Photo Annotation > Before you begin

text:
Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools
Zuper offers a comprehensive yet intuitive set of tools tailored for field service and property management needs. Here is what each one does and how to use it.

**Select Tool**

    Use this tool whenever you need to move, resize, or make changes to something you have already drawn.

    **How to use:** Click the cursor icon at the top of the toolbar, then click any annotation on the photo. You can drag it to a new spot or use the corner handles to resize it.

**Freehand Draw**

    Perfect for circling a defect, underlining a detail, or sketching a rough outline.

    **How to use:** Click the pencil icon, then click and drag on the image to draw. When you release the mouse, the stroke is placed, and the tool automatically switches back to Select mode so you can fine-tune it.

**Polyline**

    Great for tracing straight edges such as roof lines, property boundaries, or paths of damage.

    **How to use:** Click the polyline icon, then click once for each point you want to connect. Double-click when you are finished. You can later adjust its color, thickness, or delete it.

**Arrow**

    One of the most useful tools — it lets you point directly at an issue and add a label or measurement at the same time.

    **How to use:** Click the arrow icon, then click and drag to draw the arrow in the direction you want. When you release, a small window appears with four choices:

    * Free-text note (for example: "Replace this section" or "Priority: High")
    * Linear measurement in feet and inches
    * Linear measurement in metres and centimetres
    * Area measurement in square feet

    Type your information and click **Save**. The label appears neatly on the arrow, so anyone looking at the photo later will understand exactly what you mean without extra notes.

**Circle and Rectangle**

    Use the circle tool to highlight round or oval areas like holes, stains, or leaks. Use the rectangle tool for square or rectangular sections such as windows, panels, or larger areas.

    **How to use:** Click and drag to draw the shape. Once placed, you can change the color, adjust how transparent it is, add text, duplicate it, or remove it.

**Text Tool**

metadata.title: Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools

text:
Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools
Sometimes you just need a simple label on its own. Place a standalone label anywhere on the image to name an area, add an instruction, or stamp a measurement.

    **How to use:** Click the **T** icon in the left toolbar.

    1. Click the desired location on the photo. The text input box appears.
    2. Choose the appropriate mode from the tabs at the top:
       * **Abc** — Free-form text (e.g., "Replace gutter section", "Priority High")
       * **ft. in.** — Linear measurement in feet and inches
       * **m. cm.** — Linear measurement in metres and centimetres
       * **sq. ft.** — Area measurement in square feet
    3. Enter the content and click **Save**.

    You can move, resize, or edit the text later.

**Magnifier**

    Need to show a tiny detail without losing the bigger picture?

    **How to use:** Click the magnifying glass icon and then click on the area you want to zoom in on. A circular magnified view appears at 4× zoom. You can move it around or adjust the zoom level as needed.

**Sticker**

    Apply a quick visual indicator without typing.

    **How to use:** Click the sticker icon, pick one from the collection (such as a check mark or flag), and click on the photo to place it. You can move or delete stickers easily.

**Quick Actions on Selected Annotations**

When you click any annotation to select it, a quick menu appears directly above it. This menu gives you fast control over that specific annotation. Here is what you can do:

* **Color picker**: Change the color of the annotation to make it stand out better.
* **Thickness picker**: Adjust how regular or solid the annotation appears so it blends nicely or draws strong attention.
* **Text (T)**: Edit or add a text label attached to the annotation.
* **Edit**: Modify the path or shape of the annotation if you need to adjust its form.
* **Duplicate**: Create an exact copy of the annotation. This is especially useful when you want to repeat the same measurement or marking across multiple areas quickly.
* **Delete**: Remove the annotation from the canvas completely.

**Adjusting and Improving Your Photo**

Before you start adding marks, you can improve the quality of the image itself:

metadata.title: Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools

text:
Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools
**Rotate 90°**

    Click this icon to turn the entire photo 90 degrees clockwise until it looks right.

**Flip Horizontal or Vertical**

    Mirror the image left to right or top to bottom.

**Crop**

    Click the **crop** icon and drag the handles to keep only the important part of the photo, then confirm.

**Adjustments**

    Click the **sliders** icon at the bottom of the toolbar. Here you can change brightness, contrast, and saturation. Move the sliders and watch the photo update live. It is usually best to make these adjustments first so your annotations look clear and professional.

Tip:
  **Tip:** Run Adjustments first, before adding any markups. Improving image clarity upfront makes your annotations easier to place accurately and easier for others to read.

**Menu bar at the Top**

At the top of the editor, you will also see menu buttons that make your workflow smoother:

* **Reset All**: Clears everything you have added so you can start fresh (this cannot be undone).
* **Save**: Applies your changes directly to the original photo.
* **Save as Copy**: Creates a new annotated version while keeping the original photo untouched. This option is especially useful when you want to keep clean before-and-after records.
* **Zoom** controls let you get a closer or wider view as you work.

**Saving and Finding Your Work**

When you are happy with your annotations, choose either **Save** or **Save as Copy** from the top bar. Your annotated photo will be added to the Gallery automatically. It will also appear in photo feeds, and anywhere else the image is used in Zuper.
You can always reopen an annotated image later to make additional changes, including adding new annotations, adjusting existing ones, or removing previously added annotations. This flexibility helps keep your records accurate as the job progresses.

Here are a few important things to remember:

metadata.title: Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools

text:
Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools
* If you use **Save as Copy**, the original photo stays exactly as it was. This is helpful for insurance claims, warranty records, or when you need to show the unchanged starting point.
* If you close the editor without clicking **Save** or **Save as Copy**, all your work will be lost.
* Using **Reset All** removes every annotation and adjustment at once.

metadata.title: Photo Annotation > Using the Annotation Tools

text:
Photo Annotation > FAQs
**Q: Will saving overwrite my original photo?**

    It depends on which option you choose. Save commits the annotations to the existing image. Save as Copy creates a new annotated version while leaving the original untouched. Use Save as Copy whenever you need to maintain a clean original for insurance, warranty, or dispute records.

**Q: How do I remove all annotations at once? **

    Click **Reset All** in the top-right corner and confirm. This removes all annotations and image adjustments in one step and cannot be undone once confirmed.

**Q: If a checklist has a single image property, what happens when I annotate and save using Save as Copy? **

    The annotated image is saved as a new copy and does not replace the original checklist image. The original remains intact. You can view both the original and the annotated version in the Gallery.

**Q: What happens if I close the editor without saving? **

    Any annotations you have placed are discarded. Your original image remains unchanged. Always click **Save** or **Save as Copy** before closing if you want to keep your work.

text:
Set up communications
> Keep your roofing team and customers connected with calls and texts built right into Zuper.

> Keep every conversation with your customers and crews in one place.

Roofing work moves constantly between the office, the field, and the customer's front door. Homeowners call about leaks, leads follow up on quotes, and crews check in from the job site throughout the day.

When these conversations happen across personal phones and separate apps, details get lost, and follow-ups slip through the cracks. Zuper Connect keeps every call and text inside Zuper, so your team stays in touch without leaving the platform.

Your business gets a dedicated phone number and a shared inbox for calls and texts. Routing rules then send each conversation to the right person, whether that is a sales rep or a dispatcher. Every call and text stays logged against the customer record, giving your team full context to continue the conversation.

Ready to get started? See the [Zuper Connect overview](https://docs.zuper.co/Zuper_Connect/Overview) to set up your number, permissions, and call routing.

metadata.title: Set up communications

text:
Configuring inboxes
> Connect Gmail or Outlook mailboxes to Zuper, and decide who can see and reply to each inbox.

Your team spends hours each day writing emails outside Zuper, then copying the details back in by hand. The Email module closes that gap by bringing your mailbox directly into the platform. Once you connect your Gmail or Outlook mailbox, every message you send or receive appears right where you already work, alongside your jobs and customers.

You decide how each inbox works. Connect a personal inbox that only you can see, or set up a shared inbox that your whole team can read from and reply to together. You can connect as many inboxes as your business needs, and control exactly who has access to each one.

Not every email needs to live in Zuper, so you choose how much of it comes in. Set an inbox to sync everything it receives, or limit it to only the messages already linked to a job or a customer. Think of each connected inbox as a doorway into Zuper: you decide how wide to open it, and who gets to walk through.

Note:
  Learn more about how connected emails appear on jobs and customer records in **Emails in jobs and customer records**.

metadata.title: Configuring inboxes

text:
Configuring inboxes > Create a new inbox
**Path:** **Settings** > **Communication** > **Email**

1. Select **Settings** from the left navigation menu.
2. Select **Communication**, then select **Email**. The **Manage Inboxes** page opens.
3. Select **+ New Inbox**.

Note:
  If you have not connected an inbox yet, the **Manage Inboxes** page appears empty. Select **+ New Inbox** to set up your first one.

4. Under **Inbox Type**, select **Personal** or **Shared**. A personal inbox is visible only to you, while a shared inbox is visible to the teams or users you choose.
5. Enter a name for the inbox in the **Inbox Name** field. Zuper displays this name wherever the inbox appears across the platform.
6. Under **Email Access**, select **Full inbox** to sync every email from this mailbox, or select **Zuper-linked emails only** to sync only the emails already linked to a job or a customer.
7. Under **Preferred Color**, select a color. Zuper uses this color as the accent for the inbox list.

metadata.title: Configuring inboxes > Create a new inbox

text:
Configuring inboxes > Create a new inbox > Add access for a shared inbox
If you selected **Shared** as the **Inbox Type**, additional access controls appear. Set these up before you connect to the mailbox.

1. Under **Roles**, select **+ Add roles** to give access to everyone who has a chosen role.
2. Under **Individual Users**, select **+ Add users** to give access to specific people, in addition to role-based access.
3. Select **Edit User Permissions** to control what each person can do with the inbox.
4. In the **Edit User Permissions** dialog, turn on **View**, **Send**, or **Notifications** for each member.

Note:
  Enable **View** permission before you enable **Send** permission. If a member does not have **View** access, that member cannot send emails from this inbox.

5. Select **Update** to save the permissions.

metadata.title: Configuring inboxes > Create a new inbox > Add access for a shared inbox

text:
Configuring inboxes > Create a new inbox > Connect your mailbox
After you enter the inbox details, connect the mailbox that the inbox will sync with.

1. Select **Save and Connect**. The **Connect a new mailbox** dialog opens.
2. Select **Google** or **Microsoft** as your email provider.
3. Enter your email address in the **Email** field.

Note:
  Zuper checks whether this email address is already connected, by you or by another member of your team.

4. Select **Authenticate**. A sign-in window from Google or Microsoft opens.
5. Select your email account from the list, or select **Use another account** to sign in with a different one.
6. Enter your password, if prompted. Zuper skips this step if you are already signed in to the selected account. Grant Zuper the requested permissions, and select **Allow** for each one.
7. Select **Next** to complete the sign-in.

Note:
  Outlook and Microsoft 365 mailboxes connect the same way. Select **Microsoft** instead of **Google** on the **Connect a new mailbox** dialog, then sign in with your Microsoft account. If you select **Skip** instead, Zuper discards the mailbox connection step, and you can connect the mailbox later from the **Manage Inboxes** page.

Once connected, the inbox shows a **Connected** status on the **Manage Inboxes** page, along with the email account it is linked to.

metadata.title: Configuring inboxes > Create a new inbox > Connect your mailbox

text:
Configuring inboxes > Manage your inboxes
All your inboxes appear together on the **Manage Inboxes** page, where you can review and update them at any time.

1. Go to **Settings**, select **Communication**, then select **Email** to open the **Manage Inboxes** page.
2. Review the **Inbox**, **Type**, **Connected account**, **Email Access**, **Status**, and **Access** columns for each inbox.
3. Select the context menu (three-dot icon) next to an inbox to see the available actions.
4. Select **Edit** to modify the inbox details, including its name, access, and permissions.
5. Select **Revoke & Delete** to permanently remove the inbox.

Warning:
  **Revoke & Delete** permanently removes the mailbox access and the synced email history for that inbox. This action cannot be undone.

metadata.title: Configuring inboxes > Manage your inboxes

text:
Configuring inboxes > FAQs
**Can I connect more than one inbox?**

    Yes, but the number you can connect depends on your role.

    Team leads and field executives can connect one personal inbox and multiple shared inboxes. Admins can connect multiple personal and shared inboxes.

    Each inbox appears on the **Manage Inboxes** page, along with its type, connected account, and status.

**What happens when my email connection expires?**

    Zuper prompts you to reconnect using the same sign-in steps.

    Until you reconnect, the inbox is unavailable in the Communication module, and Zuper does not sync new emails.

    Existing email history on jobs and customer records remains unaffected.

**What happens when I select Revoke & Delete?**

    Zuper permanently removes the mailbox access and synced email history for that inbox, including emails linked to jobs and customers.

    This action cannot be undone.

metadata.title: Configuring inboxes > FAQs

text:
Connect a Supplier
> Order roofing materials from SRS Distribution or ABC Supply without leaving Zuper.

***Stop switching between systems to price and order materials.***

Ordering roofing materials often means leaving Zuper to check pricing elsewhere, then returning to update the job. This slow back-and-forth can cost you accuracy and time on every estimate.

Zuper connects directly to your account with SRS Distribution or ABC Supply. Once connected, live branch pricing flows straight into your estimates and material orders. Zuper refreshes this pricing every day, so your team always quotes accurate numbers.

When an order ships, delivery updates and the supplier invoice appear right on the material order. This gives your team one place to track every material from quote to delivery.

Ready to get started? If you order from SRS Distribution, see [Connect your SRS account](https://docs.zuper.co/Integrations/Purchasing/SRS-setup) to link your account.

If you order from ABC Supply, see [Connecting ABC Supply](https://docs.zuper.co/Integrations/Purchasing/abc-supply/connecting-abc-supply) to link your account instead.

metadata.title: Connect a Supplier

text:
Use Zuper on mobile
> Take your jobs, checklists, and photos with you to every roof with the Zuper mobile app.

> Everything your crew needs, right there on the roof.

Roofing work happens outside the office, on rooftops, driveways, and job sites where a laptop is not an option. Field executives need job details, checklists, and photos on hand the moment they arrive.

The Zuper mobile app puts your entire job in your pocket. You can view assigned jobs, complete inspection checklists, and capture roof photos directly from the site.

Even on a roof with weak signal, offline mode keeps you working. Every update, note, and photo syncs automatically once your device reconnects.

Ready to get started? See the [Quickstart Guide](https://docs.zuper.co/Zuper_Mobile_Apps/Quickstart-guide-for-FE) to install the app, log in, and start managing your jobs.
